title: Craft Blend 4-Mix Trio #11 (L:세로 띠·매끈 / C:부채꼴·물결 / R:동심원·물결)
prompt:
Image format: a landscape-orientation photograph, 4:5 aspect ratio.

A photograph of THREE women standing side by side on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing else in the frame, 50mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking across all of them from one side, sharp focus head to toe on each — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Left woman: a real adult Chinese woman in her mid 30s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, clear fair skin, a warm rose-red wash blended across the outer corners of both eyes and drifting up toward the temples, the same flush spreading softly across the cheekbones and the bridge of the nose, slightly smudged, dewy highlights, soft brown-pink eyeshadow, large moist eyes with bright real catchlights and a faint glassy shine, moist rose-tinted lips, a dreamy, half-lidded expression, demure and soft, warm auburn red-brown hair styled in half-up, top section lifted with the length flowing loose below, real living eyes. Long oval nails, holographic finish.

Left woman's physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person. A dramatically impossible waist-to-hip ratio dominates her silhouette: a colossal heavy bust, an extremely sharply cinched waist pulled in far tighter than the waistline of any of her other curves, and then enormous round hips flaring out to a width many times greater than that narrow waist. Gigantic soft thighs pressed together, very thick soft arms, a gigantic rounded rear. Her head looks small on top of her massive body. Not a plus-size model, not evenly proportioned. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Left woman's body art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 vertical bands by 3 hazy transition zones centred about 20% of the way across her figure from her left edge, about 37% of the way across her figure from her left edge and about 79% of the way across her figure from her left edge. Region 1 is everything to her left of the first transition zone: it is painted in Russian Palekh miniature lacquer (a deep black ground with fine gold linework and firebirds), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense jewel-toned scenework filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the strip between transition zone 1 and transition zone 2: it is painted in Ethiopian cross-and-lattice gold pattern (a deep wine-red ground with fine gold lattice linework), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense lattice linework filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the strip between transition zone 2 and transition zone 3: it is painted in Yoruba adire eleko pattern (a deep indigo ground with bold cream resist-painted geometric motifs), wide cream bands following the contours of the body, dense geometric bird motifs filling the space between bands. Region 4 is everything to her right of the last transition zone: it is painted in Japanese maki-e gold-powder lacquer (a deep glossy black urushi lacquer ground scattered with a traditional motif — cherry blossoms, cranes among pine, or maple leaves — rendered in fine sprinkled gold powder), wide gold-powder bands following the contours of the body, dense gold powder glittering densely filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a smooth, even, straight course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Left woman's pose: full side profile, one arm reaching forward, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Left woman's footwear: extreme ballet heels, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Center woman: a real adult Thai woman in her mid 20s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, flawless pale-golden skin, sharply defined dark brows, a precise black winged liner with a strong flick, warm brown-bronze eyeshadow, long dramatic lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, strong contour under the cheekbones, deep red glossy lips with a crisp edge, a poised, dramatic expression, demure and soft, deep dark brown hair styled in natural curls gathered into a high rounded puff, real living eyes. Long coffin nails, chrome finish.

Center woman's physique: An enormous, overwhelmingly muscular woman. Massive thick arms with heavy defined muscle, a broad powerful muscular back, a huge powerful chest, a heavy dense muscular torso and legs, only a soft hint of a waistline. Enormous round hips and colossal thick thighs with muscle visible through a soft layer, thick heavy calves. Not slim, not lean. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Center woman's body art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 wedge-shaped regions radiating from a single centre point located about 59% of the way down her figure from the top on the centre line of her figure. 4 hazy ray-shaped transition zones leave that centre pointing toward 9 o'clock, 11 o'clock, 2 o'clock and 6 o'clock as seen by the camera, where 12 o'clock points straight up. Region 1 is the wedge between the 9 o'clock ray and the 11 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it is painted in Spanish Andalusian filigree (a deep black ground with fine silver filigree in geometric star patterns), wide silver bands following the contours of the body, dense geometric star filigree filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the wedge between the 11 o'clock ray and the 2 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it is painted in Korean najeon mother-of-pearl lacquer (glossy black lacquer with shimmering mother-of-pearl vines), wide mother-of-pearl bands following the contours of the body, dense scrollwork filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the wedge between the 2 o'clock ray and the 6 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it is painted in Islamic geometric star-tile pattern (a dense precise pattern of interlocking eight-pointed stars), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense geometric star-and-polygon tile filling the space between bands. Region 4 is the wedge between the 6 o'clock ray and the 9 o'clock ray, sweeping clockwise: it is painted in Norwegian rosemaling folk painting (a deep forest-green ground with bold cream and gold acanthus scrollwork), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense acanthus scrollwork filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a gently undulating wave, rising and falling softly, rather than a straight course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Center woman's pose: both hands sweeping her hair back, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Center woman's footwear: extreme platform stiletto studded boots, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Right woman: a real adult Chinese woman in her early 50s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, porcelain-pale skin, slender upswept willow-leaf brows, a fine red floral huadian mark painted on the forehead, softly flushed rosy cheeks, an upswept eyeliner tail, large eyes with bright real catchlights, a small vivid red lip, a serene expression, cool and composed, soft pastel-mint-green hair styled in many small bantu knots covering the scalp, real living eyes. Long oval nails, glossy finish.

Right woman's physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person. Huge rounded shoulders and thick, powerfully muscular arms with the swell of the muscle visible beneath a soft layer, a colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size. Below that waistline a great mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and drops down under its own weight, gathering into two or three heavy rounded folds, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, not pregnant. Enormous round hips more than three times the width of that waistline, colossal thighs with a muscular sweep visible beneath the fat, thick heavy calves. Her head looks small on top of her massive body. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Right woman's body art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 concentric regions around a single centre point located about 59% of the way down her figure from the top on the centre line of her figure, separated by 3 hazy ring-shaped transition zones at about 32%, 52% and 67% of the way out from that centre point to the farthest edge of her figure. Region 1 is the innermost core around the centre point: it is painted in Portuguese azulejo tile (a brilliant white ground with deep cobalt-blue floral borders), wide cobalt bands following the contours of the body, dense repeating panel scrollwork filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the ring between transition zone 1 and transition zone 2: it is painted in Egyptian Mamluk brass-and-enamel inlay (a deep black ground with fine gold and silver geometric star inlay), wide gold-and-silver bands following the contours of the body, dense geometric star inlay filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the ring between transition zone 2 and transition zone 3: it is painted in Spanish Talavera de la Reina ceramic (a warm ivory ground with cobalt-blue and ochre floral medallions), wide cobalt bands following the contours of the body, dense floral medallion border filling the space between bands. Region 4 is the outermost region beyond the last ring: it is painted in Nigerian Adire indigo resist-dye (a deep indigo-blue ground with bold white resist-dyed motifs), wide white bands following the contours of the body, dense spiral resist motifs filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a gently undulating wave, rising and falling softly, rather than a perfectly circular course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Right woman's pose: both hands sweeping her hair back, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Right woman's footwear: extreme platform thigh-skimming boots, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Composition: each woman's own pose as described, inner arms not crossing her neighbours, all faces toward the camera.

Lighting: the blended painted patterns reading crisp against each woman's skin, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D, 4:5 8K.
